newsitem.title: USA: Bomb scare halts rush-hour traffic in Atlanta.
newsitem.headline: Bomb scare halts rush-hour traffic in Atlanta.

text.p: A report of a suspicious gym bag along a 12-lane interstate highway tied up morning rush-hour traffic for more than an hour Monday in a city already shaken by three bombings in seven months.
The bag contained only clothing but the scare snarled traffic for miles along Interstate 85, which connects Atlanta with the metropolitan area's populous northern suburbs.

Police said an agent for the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms spotted a nylon gym bag next to the concrete median wall along the highway's southbound lanes. The agent told police the bag looked as if it contained something rigid, like the components of a bomb.

Since the Feb. 22 bombing of a gay and lesbian nightclub in Atlanta, local police have discovered pipe bombs along highways in two suburban counties. "We had to be careful," Dekalb County police spokesman Chuck Johnson said.

After receiving the ATF agent's report at about 7 a.m. EST, Dekalb police cut off southbound traffic on the interstate. About 90 minutes later, the local bomb squad announced that the incident had been a false alarm.
"All they found in the bag was gym clothing. We don't know where it came from or how it got there," Johnson said.
Commuter traffic, which was backed up into the next county by the obstruction, took the better part of an hour to clear.

Along with last month's nightclub bombing, Atlanta area police and federal officials have been investigating a January bomb attack on a local abortion clinic and last July's deadly Centennial Olympic Park bombing in downtown Atlanta.

All told, two people have died and more than 120 have been injured as a result of the three bombings, which all remain unsolved. The Centennial Olympic Park and nightclub bombings involved devices that had been concealed in backpacks.
